Hi Liina, 

These third-party insurance companies started reaching out to us years back for two reasons: 

1. To assist drivers to claim vehicle damages after being involved in an accident. They would like to confirm if the vehicle/driver was operating during the time of the accident. 
2. Confirm if the vehicle is registered on our platform because some drivers/vehicle owners do not disclose that they are using the vehicle to transport passengers so in order to pay a cheaper premium. 

Since we saw numerous companies reach out, we created a process on how to handle these and respond to them to maintain a good relationship so that Bolt drivers do not have issues when they want to take a cover with them. Most important we do not confirm anything without a consent letter signed by the vehicle owner allowing them to request such information. 

Just to re-iterate, Tshwarelo Malakalaka confirmed that the vehicle was on our platform before receiving the consent letter. Thabane Msomi confirmed that the vehicle and driver are registered on our platform and confirmed that the vehicle was in use on the day of the accident. Due to this the insurance company did not pay for the vehicle damages which prompted the driver to enquire why we shared this information without his consent.

*About the ticket:* 
The intention of the request are at first my curiosity and second to understand the customer journey (in addition to my first request last year: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nf9GUCBn_LK_UbX6EAKYjvEsEsYQgkk1mdRiFyDhwLo/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nf9GUCBn_LK_UbX6EAKYjvEsEsYQgkk1mdRiFyDhwLo/edit|smart-link] ) The inability to provide the data is one of the existing areas for improvement (among others), but I also understand that it is not a business-critical priority to fix this. But it should definitely be on the to-do list when we look at the DSAR process. 

*About closing the ticket:*

* A response was always given within one day
* CS provided the JSON file inApp within 2 days.
* CS was very polite and pleasant
* When I asked about the specific recipients, CS explicitly referred me to the privacy notice and the list of recipient categories.

Hey [~accountid:637dde429960988ef6bdc382] !

Storing data for the purpose of creating a talent pool and contacting them with offers to other roles is an entirely new processing purpose from storing the data for possible claims. 

If we would like to store and use the data to contact in case of new offers in the future, then that requires asking separate consent. 

So the logic would be the following: 
a) unsuccessful candidate personal data would be deleted after the default retention period set based on limitation period of possible claims stipulated in law (6months-1year based on market specifics); 

b) if the candidate has separately consented to the retention of their data for receiving future offers, then the data is deleted after the withdrawal of such consent or after a maximum period of 3 years. 

This consent can be asked in the job application itself or separately from a candidate. Either way we have to keep an overview of such consents given and offer the opportunity to withdraw the consent by the candidates. 

Let me know if this is something we would be ready to implement, so that we can look into where and how to add the consent  + update the privacy notice regarding this. 

The referral to our privacy notice is now updated in our careers page. 

Liis

Hi!

*1.What is the purpose of this tool.?*

Sorry for my unclear explanation of this topic. _Of course, if the partner doesn’t pay us, primarily we use payouts termination._ Switching is like an additional tool. I think, this topic is more complex, I will try to cover it more widely.

All our partners are divided into two types of legal entities -  limited liability companies (Ltd) and private entrepreneurs (PE). These types vary due to volumes of their turnover and so on. Most of our partners are PE and operate in Simplified Tax system (STS). Ltds can be only on General Tax system, all such partners are on the Net Settlement scheme. The net-off in payment is not allowed under the STS, because restaurants must show 100% sales in their tax declaration. 

Since the beginning of the martial law in Ukraine, quite a lot of companies have been forced to temporarily suspend work, especially in those cities of Ukraine, where such work was impossible due to the military actions of the Russian Federation. Given the difficult circumstances for business, the government allowed a number of taxpayers to switch to the STS, including Ltds. It was made for supporting Ukraine's economy and to help the business that continues operating in such hard times for our country. 

Therefore, some big Ltd-partners, like KFC, Пузата Хата etc., switched from General to Simplified taxation system. In this regard we moved them from Net to Gross scheme (according to their requests). When martial law ends, _there is a big probability that all of them will return back to the General taxation system. So from our side correct transitioning from Gross to Net scheme also will be needed._

*2.What about communication, if we change their invoicing method without their consent, do we inform them by email/notification or something.?*

We don’t change anything without informing partner, especially settlement approach. 



I hope I didn't confuse you even more. Let me know, if you need more details.



Thanks.

Summarising the ticket details again for both financial controlling, and documentation purposes.

*Business Requirement:* the operations teams require on each inventory item to have a “usage limit per repair” to specify how much each mechanic can select the maximum amount on the Charger App screen. By default it is set to 12. There is the additional requirement to have some business critical items, such as IOTs, to limit to 1 per repair. 

*Business Solution:* to achieve this, within Workday we can configure additional *Item Identifiers* which can then be assigned to spend categories, then items accordingly. These item identifiers are most often used for Universal Commodity Codes (i.e. custom codes) however due to the free text field we can set this to anything and are therefore utilising this to input a *Max Repair Usage* identifier. This is then to be assigned to the spend category (allowing for the items, which are held against that spend category) to have this value input. 



This has been configured, and tested in the pre-live tenant (BOLT5) and the appropriate technical solution has been developed by Robin from the ENG Rentals team. This means that we have added a column to the Charger App report which the team receives, and limits the amount of spare parts that can be logged per repair as per report accordingly. 

Due to Financial Controlling owning the spend categories, we require the approval to go ahead with this change please.

* Inventory Spare Parts
* Inventory Fixed Asset Components

The Integration report then has an additional columns, with max repair usage value. If it is blank, then it defaults to 12 or if it’s input then it takes that value in the app to limit the usage amount as per business requirement.

Notes:

* ICC cannot be aggregated to different levels, which is anyways ok considering tests are usually inferred at city level. 
* ICC is based on estimation of random-effects variance which is not supported in spark so data has to be loaded into memory.
* We can calculate ICC for each city once a month on 2 weeks data using LMMs and store the variance inflation factor to the city-level sample size data.

*What has been checked:*

* City areas data pipeline and main thread profiling (micromobility + carsharing)
* Markers data pipeline and main thread profiling (micromobility + carsharing)
* Availability of markers batch rendering by Google Maps

*Summary:*

* Both city areas and markers data pipelines are well optimised already, but there are some possibilities for small improvements
* Sometimes Google maps was freezing a bit even though app had stable 60 fps (main thread was not loaded), meaning that Google maps can freeze in its separate thread and we can’t control it. This happened while moving camera with a lot of city areas added to the map, the more areas, the worse was the lag. It may be related to synchronising map and polygon layers positions inside Google maps sdk and it’s possible that we will face this too with custom renderer if we want to synchronise map layers positions. Or maybe it relates to absence of batch drawing inside Google maps.
* Markers in carsharing are reusing same Google maps image descriptor for all vehicles of same model, so if there’s a batch rendering inside Google maps, it should be already working

*Potential city areas improvements:*

* {{ObserveCityAreasInteractor}} - don't reload city areas from db if tile ids didn't change (doesn't affect main thread and fps)
* {{ObserveRentalsCityAreasInteractor}} - use single observable(flow) for all map-related data: zoom, location bounds, viewport. Multiple map data observables emit simultaneously when map position changes which leads to unnecessary work (doesn't affect main thread and fps)

*Potential markers improvements:*

* {{CarsharingVehicleMapRibInteractor}} - move pre-order vehicles models mapping to worker thread (affects main thread, but according to profiler, not significantly)
* {{CarsharingVehicleMapRibInteractor}} - update markers only when map is idle. It works in micromobility this way, but in carsharing we have different marker types based on zoom level, so need to figure out how to make it appropriately from UX side (affects main thread significantly during map zoom and move)
* Minimise {{GoogleMap.getCameraPosition}} calls (see map improvements section). Problem happens during markers zoom
* {{ZoomGoogleMarkerInvalidator}} - introduce batching of marker invalidate actions, like in {{MapActionBatchProcessor}}. Currently during zoom all added markers are invalidated at once on main thread.
* {{CarsharingObservePreOrderMapVehiclesInteractor}} - Improve filtering by viewport logic. Either use different viewport paddings for different zoom levels (and configure vertical/horizontal paddings separately), or filter markers that intersect with viewport (calculate marker location bounds). Filter viewport paddings were introduced here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/RNTL-12550|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/RNTL-12550|smart-link] 

*Potential map improvements:*

* Minimise {{GoogleMap.getCameraPosition}} calls. Profiler showed that such calls happen a lot in the app during map interaction (especially during zooming with a lot of markers) and they take noticeable amount of main thread time. Seems that we can cache latest map position and avoid making expensive Google maps sdk calls. But this will require significant amount of refactoring

Local counsel (Ecija) confirmed that *Spain can be seen as a Type 2 Country* unfortunately (same as the UK).

+Full advice below FYI+:

Please, be aware that article 35.3 of Spanish Royal Decree Law 19/2018, of November 23, on payment services and other urgent financial measures, clearly establishes that the beneficiaries of payment operations (Bolt) may not require the payer (the passenger) the payment of expenses or additional fees for the use of any payment instrument (the card).

*This local prohibition on card surcharges does not consider the intention of the charge*, +so if Bolt is going to charge the service fee only to passengers paying with card, such services fee would be deemed as a card surcharge, even though that is not Bolt’s intention to charge passengers a card surcharge+.

Further, this only applies in cases where we can’t validate that the damage was caused during an active trip with one of Bolt’s e-vehicles.

Hi everyone,

Let me some up which guidelines we are currently following.



At the moment we ask 4 different documents to register a vehicle with Bolt 🇵🇹 

# Vehicles' registration doc *

# Insurance Conditions

# Insurance Certificate (green card)

# Inspection



*If the vehicle isn't owned by the Fleet, Fleet Owner can submit the original registration doc + rental agreement 



Regarding Law 45/2018, under clause 12, we can find the vehicles' requirements:

* Capacity <= 9
* Registration Plate from Portugal
* Age <= 7 years
* Yearly Inspection after completing 1 year old
* Insurance (50.000.000 Civil Liability + 10.000 Occupant Protection)

There is no particular statement regarding the vehicle's ownership. But we do find it important to have a clear view of the company's relationship with the vehicle (to avoid for example stolen cars riding with us). If we analyse [law 291/2007|https://dre.pt/dre/detalhe/decreto-lei/291-2007-640637] clause 6 (Obligation to insure), we can conclude that:



* The obligation to insure rests with the owner of the vehicle except in cases of property reservation, usufruct, finance lease)



Assumptions:

# A legit rental agreement can be interpreted as usufruct

# When there is no legit rental agreement, usufruct should be registered on the vehicles' registration doc



What is a legit rental agreement?



Rent-a-Car (shorter periods)

* The company needs to comply with [several requirements established by IMT|https://www.imt-ip.pt/sites/IMTT/Portugues/TransportesRodoviarios/AluguerVeiculosSemCondutor/Aluguer-Ve%C3%ADculos-Passageiros/Paginas/Rent-a-car.aspx] - [Law 181/2012|https://dre.pt/dre/detalhe/decreto-lei/181-2012-178993]
* [Public list|https://www.imt-ip.pt/sites/IMTT/Portugues/TransportesRodoviarios/EmpresasLicenciadas/Documents/Empresas_Rent-a-Car_Sharing_OrdEmp.pdf] disclosed by IMT



Renting - ALD (Longer period) - Not governed by law 181/2012. Which guidelines should we follow?

{noformat}-- Driver
with driver_gmv as 
(
	select 'driver' as entity_type, driver_id as entity_id, ${date_selected} as computed_on_date,
	max("_last_ingested") as last_ingestion_timestamp, 
	sum(ride_price_eur) as gmv_eur,
	sum(ride_price_eur) as gmv_eur_rides,
	sum(cast(null as double)) as gmv_eur_scooter,
	sum(cast(null as double)) as gmv_eur_car_rental,
	sum(cast(null as double)) as gmv_eur_delivery,
	sum(finished_orders) as total_orders,
	sum(finished_orders) as total_orders_rides,
	sum(cast(null as double)) as total_orders_scooter,
	sum(cast(null as double)) as total_orders_car_rental,
	sum(cast(null as double)) as total_orders_delivery
	from ng_public.etl_driver_hourly_activity 
	where period_local_date > ${date_selected} - interval '30' day and period_local_date <= ${date_selected}
	group by 1, 2, 3
),
driver_refund as 
(
	select 'driver' as entity_type, ic.external_id as entity_id, ${date_selected} as computed_on_date,
	max(bbd.created) as last_ingestion_timestamp,
	count(bbd.balance_entry_id) as refund_count,
	sum(bbd.amount/coalesce(vcer.rate, 1)) as refund_amount_eur
	from ng_public.etl_billing_balance_driver bbd 
	left join ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates vcer on vcer.currency = bbd.currency and date(vcer.valid_on) = date(bbd.created_date)
	left join ng_public.invoicing_client ic on ic.id = bbd.entity_id and ic.type = 'Driver'
	where entity_type = 'driver' and bbd.created_date > ${date_selected} - interval '30' day and bbd.created_date <= ${date_selected}
		and transaction_type = 'compensation' and transaction_subtype in ('cs_automation', 'manual')
	group by 1, 2, 3
),
driver_data as
(
	select 'driver' as entity_type, 
	coalesce(dr.entity_id, dg.entity_id) as entity_id, 
	coalesce(dr.computed_on_date, dg.computed_on_date) as computed_on_date,
	dg.last_ingestion_timestamp as gmv_last_ingestion_timestamp,
	dr.last_ingestion_timestamp as refund_last_ingestion_timestamp,
	dg.gmv_eur,
	dg.gmv_eur_rides,
	dg.gmv_eur_scooter,
	dg.gmv_eur_car_rental,
	dg.gmv_eur_delivery,
	dg.total_orders,
	dg.total_orders_rides,
	dg.total_orders_scooter,
	dg.total_orders_car_rental,
	dg.total_orders_delivery,
	dr.refund_count,
	dr.refund_amount_eur
	from driver_gmv dg
	full outer join driver_refund dr on dr.entity_id = dg.entity_id and dr.computed_on_date = dg.computed_on_date 
),

* Being on the list means the party cannot be involved in exports, re-exports, or transfers (in-country) subject to the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), unless certain additional requirements are complied with, essentially obtaining an UVL statement from this party. * According to the BIS clarification regarding the scope of the EAR and also an article from Morgan Lewis Law Firm (both attached), items subject to the EAR are: “(1) All items in the United States, including in a U.S. Foreign Trade Zone or moving in transit through the United States from one foreign country to another; (2) All U.S. origin items wherever located; (3) Foreign-made commodities that incorporate controlled U.S.-origin commodities, foreign-made commodities that are ‘bundled’ with controlled U.S.-origin software, foreign-made software that is commingled with controlled U.S.-origin software, and foreign-made technology that is commingled with controlled U.S.-origin technology (...); (4) Certain foreign-produced “direct products” of specified “technology” and “software,” as described in § 736.2(b)(3) of the EAR; and (5) Certain foreign-produced “direct products” of a complete plant or any major component of a plant as described in § 736.2(b)(3) of the EAR.”
* Thus, services don’t seem to be subject to EAR and, as a consequence, affected by the UVL.
* Moreover, the restrictions deriving from the UVL seem to apply only to US based companies transactioning with customers listed in the UVL, and not to suppliers of EU based companies as in the case at hand. This is also corroborated by one article from Squire Patton Boggs Law Firm (attached).

Please note that 

* delivery of small packages requires licensing by the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA). Small packages are all letters,postcards, printed matter, small parcels of up to 30kg.
* Couriers are not authorised to deliver small parcels that are less than 1kg e.g letters and small parcels as these are considered only an activity that the Post Office can provide. Post Net was delivering small packages in contravention of the law and were sued by the Post Office as a result.Court issued an injunction to allow PostNet to continue rendering delivery services of small packeges until the matter is finally decided by the court. TakeAlot also jointed the PostNet Litigation. While the fight is currently with the courier companies, it is likely that the same concerns or complaintswill soon follow for the e-hailing sector rendering analogous services, albeit indirectly in the case of e-hailing companies. However, at the moment the market remains open and everyone continues to deliver small parcels i.e. <1kg pending outcome of the PostNet case. It is also unlikely that individual drivers will be adversely impacted by the prohibition on delivery of small packages as the law allows small packages to be delivered if they are for personal purposes, or for office to office deliveries, delivery of legal processes, ocassional deliveries by an individual not in the business of delivering letters.

# First, we gathered data on failed orders and aggregated them by provider_id’s. Having narrowed these down to those belonging to provider_id’s that are within our fraud weekly *thresholds* (more than 100 eur in sum of failed orders; ratios over 33% for count and sum of failed/all orders); we reached an impact assessment of *20.635 eur over 8 weeks*. The highest numbers come from *Ghana* (8.500 eur), Sweden (2.694 eur), Azerbaijan (2.523 eur) and Portugal (2.510 eur) as per the table below:

!Screenshot 2023-01-24 at 15.31.17.png|width=611,height=322!



* Query for identifying fraudulent providers:

{noformat}select date_trunc('week', o.created_date) as weeks,
      o.provider_id,
      o.country,
      round(cast(SUM(o.provider_price/r.rate)*1.000 as double),2) as sum_all_orders,
      round(cast(sum(case when o.state='failed' then o.provider_price/r.rate else 0 end)*1.000 as double),2) as sum_failed_orders,
      round((round(cast(sum(case when o.state='failed' then o.provider_price/r.rate else 0 end)*1.000 as double),2)/round(cast(SUM(o.provider_price/r.rate)*1.000 as double),2)),3) as ratio_sum_failed_orders,
      count(o.id) as count__all_orders,
      sum(case when o.state='failed' then 1 else 0 end) as count_failed_orders,
      round((sum(case when o.state='failed' then 1 else 0 end)*1.000/count(o.id)*1.000),3) as ratio_count_failed_orders
      from ng_delivery.delivery_order_order o
      LEFT JOIN ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r ON o.currency  = r.currency
          AND date_trunc('day', o.created) = date_trunc('day', r.valid_on)
      where o.created_date >= DATE(DATE_ADD('week', -9, CURRENT_DATE))
      and o.country != 'tv'
      --and o.provider_id = 48268
      group by 1,2,3
      having (round((round(cast(sum(case when o.state='failed' then o.provider_price/r.rate else 0 end)*1.000 as double),2)/round(cast(SUM(o.provider_price/r.rate)*1.000 as double),2)),3) >= 0.33
            and round((sum(case when o.state='failed' then 1 else 0 end)*1.000/count(o.id)*1.000),3) >= 0.33
            and round(cast(sum(case when o.state='failed' then o.provider_price/r.rate else 0 end)*1.000 as double),2) >= 100
            and sum(case when o.state='failed' then 1 else 0 end) > 1)
      order by 1 asc{noformat}

It’s possible to change the partitioning key, but there can be only one partition key. So the new one would replace the current one. Which also means that all other queries from other users to this table would be affected, not just yours.

If the key should still be changed, *and* it’s okay to have data for this table being unavailable for a while during the migration, you can change the partition key in the config and add a [backfill|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4049731679/How+to+setup+self-serve+replication+to+Delta+Lake#If-you-need-to-backfill-a-table] with the {{dropTableIfExists}} option set. The next ingestion run would then drop the old table, create a new one with the new partition key, and backfill all rows.

If data needs to be available all the time during the migration it’s still possible, but would require a more manual process with rewriting the data in the background.

Hi [~accountid:624407b42e101c006a8d8cf6] 

In France the procedure and the payment flow differ depending on the nature of the charges due by the user.

We can have 

*A)* *Contractual penalties and Administratives fees* ( aka any predetermined amount inserted in the table at the bottom of French T&Cs) 

User already provided consent to pay any contractual penalty within the acceptance of Bolt Drive T&Cs. Bolt can debit users' payment method subject to *prior written notification* (first template in Thiago's Legal memo with minor tweaks) to be sent via email / app notification including the following details:

* the violation,
* relevant T&Cs provision and 
* possibility to challenge our decision+ communication channel to reach out to object the decision. 

*Nota:* there’s no need to provide evidence of the damage and only the predetermined damage stated in the T&Cs can be charged. 

*B* ) *Damage claims* by Bolt to the user (mostly damages to the vehicle) → *Evidence* must be provided + *Invoice* of the fees incurred to repair the vehicle +  *User’s consent* are required before debiting the payment method. User has the right to refuse and in such a case, you need to go to court to claim refund.

*D) Public parking fines* (“_Forfaits Post-Stationnement (FPS)_” in French)

 As per [Expansion Memo|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fSagAcjvBcVAZLGiHw0M5Iq83qu6uF2u/edit] (page 11), under [+French law+|https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000043976767/], the holder of the registration certificate is liable for the payment of public parking fines. Bolt *must* therefore *pay the public parking fines on behalf of the user* but costs can be pass on to user. Bolt can debit user’s payment card of the amount of the fine (+ the management costs)  *or,* when this is not possible, the amount can be invoiced to the user who undertakes to pay them by bank transfer. Either way,  *a prior written notification* (email /in app must be sent to user including : 

* short background description
* a copy of the corresponding notice and all relevant documents to enable the user (if necessary) to file an administrative appeal.
* *Nota* the fact that the user expressly acknowledges that his/her decision to contest the fine shall not prevent Bolt from deducting a sum corresponding to the amount of the fine+ 20 euros ( contractual penalty corresponding to the costs to handle the case)  as soon as the user /Bolt is notified of the fine.

*E*) *Private parking fines* can follow the *same rules as public parking fines* although from a legal standpoint Bolt is not part to the parking contract and therefore it is not obliged to pay such fines. The contractual penalty is an obligation which is provided in the “parking contract” and under which the party who fails to perform the contract undertakes to pay an amount of money determined by the contract to the other party. However, OC in the Expansion Memo suggested  to handle private parking fines as they were public parking fines in order to avoid possible conflicts with private parking areas and to keep good relationships with them. 

*F*) *Traffic Fines*: Ops team should share the user data with the issuing authority, which will forward the fine to the user.

Hope this helps. Happy to discuss the above on a call. 

Thanks,

Michela

[~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897] and I discussed this for BE, FR, PT and ES and we have a couple of questions / points that I think are worth considering potentially for all countries:

* *Rider’s consent*: is necessary in all West Eur regions
* *Price information* - for driver and rider: Both driver and rider need to be notified of the new price before accepting such change to the initial contract / initial journey price estimation.
* *Risk of abuse*: driver can decide to add any stops without passenger being able to accept or refuse. What if it’s used by a driver as a fraud / way to commit (sexual) assault / take passenger anywhere? It’s a worst case scenario but still worth considering IMO…
* *Practical issues*: If a passenger has to orally ask a driver to make a stop and give him a new address, it implies that driver 1. understand properly the address (not always easy…) and 2. adds this address manually in the app - while potentially driving? Which is forbidden in West Eur countries.

In our view, a consent tick / box should be implemented so the rider can accept this new destination and new price, once proposed by the driver.

Otherwise, only the passenger’s feature should be implemented: if passenger wants an additional stop, he should request it in the app and then be able to see the additional fare involved and proceed or refuse to proceed for that additional stop once properly informed about additional price. And in such case, it should be an offer (with relevant price information) coming from the passenger that driver should have the right to accept or reject.

Let me know should you wish to discuss further or how we should proceed from there / inform our CMs etc.

Thanks

Clause 3 provides that the parties may terminate the agreement by notifying the other party via _“notificación fehaciente”._ 

A notification is considered “fehaciente” when there is proof both of its content and of the fact that the addressee has received the notification, as well as the date of receipt by the addressee. The most common forms of notification are the burofax and the notarial summons.

In short, I recommend sending the termination notice via burofax (it can be done online). I believe [~accountid:60cb48dc758a5d006a07896b] has already done it in the past. Otherwise you can ask Esther Sánchez to organise it.

*Meeting notes with Models Lifecycle team (Nadezhda Kiriushkina, Stanislau Hluboki, Alexey Ermolaev), 25.01.2023*

*Main points*

* real-time data can be ingested to Profiling either by:
** saving data in a specific S3 bucket (Profiling will subscribe to notification events on that bucket)
** sending events to Kafka or SNS/SQS and setting Profiling to consume those events
* when consuming events from Kafka or SNS/SQS, Profiling cannot perform aggregations on the data. It needs to receive data in the form in which it should be ingested. If we need to ingest aggregated data, we need to aggregate data before it comes to Profiling, e.g. by leveraging Spark Structured Streaming APIs or Kafka Streams. One possible option is also storing aggregated data on the model side.
* current ingestion lag for surge data on the Profiling side is ~1 s (which is well enough)
* currently, 7 days of surge data is stored in Profiling (key is cell_id and 10-min time interval)

*Discussed design ideas*

* Data Capture logs → Spark streaming job → S3 profiling bucket → Ingestion to Profiling (current state)
* Model Invoker → Event buffer → S3 → Spark streaming job → S3 profiling bucket → Ingestion to Profiling (might be too slow)
* Perform, store and expose aggregations on the model side → (polling) → Ingestion to Profiling (might not scale well to new data and other use cases)
* Model Invoker → Kafka or SNS/SQS → Ingestion to Profiling (issues with aggregation)
* Model Invoker → Kafka or SNS/SQS → Spark streaming job → S3 profiling bucket → Ingestion to Profiling
* Model Invoker → Kafka → aggregations in Kafka Streams → Ingestion to Profiling

*Actions on my side*

* Research the above design ideas
* What benefits we get from Kafka vs. SNS/SQS?
* Can we use Kafka Streams to aggregate data directly in the stream so the consumer (Profiling) receives already aggregated data? Does Kafka Streams meet our reliability, latency and volume requirements?
* How much data do we need for model retraining?

There are three ways of fixing it:

# we will listen to {{CHARGEBACK}} events, if Payments have it and mark our payment correspondingly,
# Payments may just accept refund for charged back payment without error (money was returned to user anyway),
# Payments may throw exception with some meaningful error code, so we will understand that it was charged back.

But for chargeback events we have two options to do:

# we can process chargebacks as refunds, in this case we will not take money from user’s balance,
# or we can process them as failed payments — user didn’t pay for the order, and in this case we need to take money for the order from balance.

And this should be a business decision what and when to do.

Currently, we don’t listen for chargeback events, which effectively works as refunds: money is returned to user, and user doesn’t get debt for the order.

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], 

I would also agree with [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] here and this was also why I initially was hesitant to approve this for the Nordic countries before I did my research. See some additional perspectives below: 

* *Contract change*: the transportation service contract is entered into between the parties based on local laws and in order for such contract to be established there needs to be an offer and acceptance. A change of contract requires a new offer and acceptance in order for such change to be valid (both parties need to agree to the change). 
* *Price change*: The price is considered to be part of the initial contract and in order to change this the rules regarding contract change need to be followed. Additionally, the rules regarding price information need to be followed which requires that both parties are aware of the price and that it is clearly stated in order for both parties to accept such price. 
* *Consent*: Regardless if the driver or rider requests to add another stop, the other party must explicitly approve such change. In general, oral consent can be sufficient in order to enter into a valid contract but we would have no evidence of the consent (hence my question on slack re how we would handle such cases). Additionally, having all contracts in the app (through offer and acceptance) and suddenly not having evidence for the full chain of acceptance would most likely be considered unreasonable based on market practice. We are arguing that the transportation service agreement is entered into between the driver and rider (and not Bolt) but if we don’t ensure that we have explicit consent from both parties in this case, Bolt may be held liable for not providing the correct measures for entering into a legally valid contract and we could in extreme cases be reported to the Consumer Agency (unlikely but still a risk). 

Happy to discuss this further as well but based on this I would highly recommend to include a consent button for the driver/rider depending on who has requested the change. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Hey [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] and [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7], thanks a lot for your detailed overview, super helpful. Initially my thinking was similar to yours but then I figured we have some additional features in the app that changed my mind. I will try to illustrate them below.

* *Offer and acceptance*
** When rider is ordering a ride, then we offer him/her an upfront price, i.e. price that rider will be paying for a ride;
** When you click on such price before placing the offer, another screen pops up that breaks down the upfront fare, shows price per km, wait time, cancellation fee and seats in the car. In addition, there is a disclaimer below which says that the upfront price may change *if the journey changes or deviates materially from the estimation, or if tolls apply.* Please see the screenshot of such screen below (see screen 1).
**  In my mind this disclaimer is part of an offer made by the driver to the rider. When rider accepts the offer, then rider also accepts the fact that the upfront price may deviate, depending on circumstances pertaining to the rider. 
* *Concluding the contract between rider and driver*
** Once the the offer is accepted, the contract between the rider and the driver is concluded on terms described on the screen with upfront price and on the screen which clarifies how this upfront price is calculated and what happens if the deviations apply.
* *Amendment of the contract between the rider and the driver*
** If rider asks for a stop in the middle of the ride, then rider makes an offer to amend the contract between the rider and the driver.
** As you see, we have informed the rider what such amendment will cost at the offer stage of the contract. Meaning wait time fee shown on the screen will apply to the amended ride. The rider has accepted the wait time fee and its possible application at the initial stage of the offer.
** Since we have shown the rider what this amendment of the contract will cost, the rider makes an informed decision of what this amendment of the contract will cost him / her.
** Once driver has accepted rider’s request to amend the contract orally, driver should make an amendment to the contract in the app by entering another stop to the app.
** Once entered, the screen below (see screen 2) is shown to the rider which shows to the rider that (i) the destination of the rider has been updated and (ii) the new price for the ride has changed. The amendment to the contract is considered to be concluded.



* *Concerns regarding the evidence of rider’s request*
** My understanding is that we don’t need to have evidence of rider’s request for a stop, since:
*** this is a contract between the rider and the driver which Bolt is not part of,
*** if rider has any concerns, he is invited to approach CS which almost every time will be granted a refund.
* *Why there is no consent built in the app and why it wouldn’t make sense in product’s opinion?*
** The driver is invited to use this feature when rider is not entering an additional stop to the app himself / herself (rider is not capable to do so, doesn’t know how to do that)
** The rider might not be likely to accept the change (because he / she doesn’t know how to do that), however, the stop is still made, and driver wants to get remunerated for that.

* *Price information* - for driver and rider: Both driver and rider need to be notified of the new price before accepting such change to the initial contract / initial journey price estimation.

I think this part is missing from driver side if rider adds a stop. Driver gets notified, but we do not have confirmation (new acceptance screen or any other format) present. 

Overall in case of a stop, it is not possible to inform about the final price in front as no one knows how long the stop will be. It has to be only information about the fair for both parties.



* *Risk of abuse*: driver can decide to add any stops without passenger being able to accept or refuse. What if it’s used by a driver as a fraud / way to commit (sexual) assault / take passenger anywhere? It’s a worst case scenario but still worth considering IMO…
* What if it’s used by a driver as a fraud - we have fraud monitoring driver patterns as well as CS solution for riders. 
* This feature will not have effects on assault as driver doesn’t need to add a paid stop to commit an assault. Assault is the worst act and for sure driver doesn’t want to add exact time and location information for it into the app.



* *Practical issues*: If a passenger has to orally ask a driver to make a stop and give him a new address, it implies that driver 1. understand properly the address (not always easy…) and 2. adds this address manually in the app - while potentially driving? Which is forbidden in West Eur countries.

True. Expectation is always that rider adds the stop. If they don’t, it becomes an issue for a driver. Driver can add the stop to their current location or type an address. It doesn’t need to happen during the driving and is not expected to happen during the driving. Same way as with destination change that is live.



* *Price change*: The price is considered to be part of the initial contract and in order to change this the rules regarding contract change need to be followed. Additionally, the rules regarding price information need to be followed which requires that both parties are aware of the price and that it is clearly stated in order for both parties to accept such price.

How can we have rider side live if this is the case? 

Is overall narrative that knowing about the change + fair sufficient? 



*I would highly recommend to include a consent button for the driver/rider depending on who has requested the change.*

This is planned for the future to enable markets that we can not do it for now. 

Would like to launch markets with no issues earlier and get these situation solved for drivers (many requests coming and it is common proposal in forums). 

With consent button we will have better solution in place, but in practice not all issues will not go away as what should driver do if rider disagrees with the change? Wait for free or end the ride on the spot or just drive forward (even if rider wants a stop)? All of them are rather conflicting situations, especially nr 3. Right now drivers wait for free and it is causing dissatisfaction.

Launching in more countries would also expose the actual reach of these situations, where rider doesn’t agree (expect these not to be high as rider side feature is now live as well and we definitely need to communicate to drivers as well that rider should be the first one adding a stop).





We will wait for updates from you before any further live releases.

# *What was the goal of the project? What actually happened? Were we accurate in predicting efforts?*

Goal: Since the L&D team has shifted its support from markets specifically to regions to maximise the impact of the work, we will establish monthly syncs with FD L&D Leads and CS FD Regional Leads, in order to offer support to the region, exchange information and agree on the possible actions.

# Feeback from the RL and this was a success - they had positive feedback regarding the whole project and would like to continue with it, maybe with few changes (more in the improvement section)
# FD market KPIs - Maintenance or increase in region’s KPIs health - this cannot be measured, as Looker is undergoing through structural changes, so we do not have the data.

We were accurate with predicting effort and the project was completed on time. But, we did not get much work from the RL side, as in - the whole project was more focused in the on of exchanging the information and mutual awareness, instead of L&D getting actual tasks from the RLs. But, this is also because of the structural changes of CS that were happening throughout the year.

*2. What went well?*

* The initial thought was to have 2 RL syncs: 1) Nigel and Masego and 2)Irena and Joshua. The reasoning is that Joshua started shortly after RL syncs had started. It was later decided to combine the sessions because:
* It would make no sense to duplicate the information being shared as they would be similar and later discussed with their respective colleagues (i.e Nigel => Irena and Masego => Joshua.
* It gave us a chance to get to know both RLs and Joshua and the opportunity to gain a better understanding of what we do.
* CS FD L&D received useful information that helped us prep for any changes that were yet to be made public and allowed us sufficient time to get ready.
* Having the 4 of us on the call, resulted in open transparency and avoidance of any misinformation sharing.
* RLs open the call platform to STLs. This gave them the option to join the calls and address any specific issues that were prevalent in the market/s.
* While we only managed to find a perfect setting on how we wanted syncs to proceed, it maintained consistency from approx. Q3.
* After publishing the notes with the rest of the KM team, we received a lot of comments and feedback based on each month’s discussion topics.
* Overall, all participants felt that the calls provided value and agreed to hopefully have them continue but under a different format (more info on improvements).

*3. What didn’t go well?*

* There were some on-and-off issues related to the Confluence page, specifically with editing access (mostly Joshua).
* Agenda notes were not published by RLs nor further documentation on the Confluence page as agreed. As a result, it felt very one-sided.
* Not all STLs took up the opportunity to join the calls. And if they did, no agenda or discussion points were shared prior to the call. This led to the discussion exceeding the time limit and context would need to be provided in the call.
* A fair amount of points raised pointed in the direction of other sub-teams, like the content. This did not relate to L&D.
* We did not have(or very limited) tasks/trainings for L&D coming from these meetings. It felt more like transferring information to the rest of the KM team. This meant that only 50% of the project's key objectives were met (exchanging information and agreeing on possible actions).
* Some months did not have much to add or comment on (from the L&D side). This was also made difficult not knowing what the RLs would bring to the call. Even after several reminders.

*4. How to avoid it next time and what can be improved?*

* Changing the frequency of the calls
* Set up a Slack workflow for adding agenda points
* Possibly create a Slack channel that allows RLs, STLs, and KM teams to engage each with other.
* Assess roadmaps and decide/agree on types of support we can provide each other (linked to business goals).

# *Why do we take such an approach and what do we benefit from this.* 
The following is an internal comment and not meant to be shared with the customer. Being deemed as separate controller is beneficial for Bolt in order not to be subject to processor’s obligations which are usually very extensive and strict. Being deemed as a data processor means that we can only process data on behalf of the controller (customer) and under their instructions. In practice this would bring us obligations such as: 
- implementing technical and organisational measures stipulated by the controller;
- being subject to controller’s audits;
- deleting the data when requested by the controller;
- restrictions on appointing sub-processors (e.g. where we store data, which service providers we use etc). 

Bolt might not be able to fulfil such obligations and we would open up ourselves to possible disputes of non-compliance as a processor. 
# *Why we are not treated as data processor?* 
The following can be used as an external explanation. 
The fact that one organisation provides a service to another organisation does not necessarily mean that it is acting as a data processor. It could be a data controller in its own right, depending on the degree of control it exercises over the processing operation. Bolt as a controller decides the means and purposes for processing the data in order to provide the service (Bolt Business to the Customer). Bolt is the one registering and administering the users, providing the platform, providing the opportunity for end-users to make use of Bolt Business in the limits set by Customers. Therefore the data being shared is for each parties separate purposes - Bolt determines the means and purposes in order to provide the services and Customer determines the means and purposes of the shared data on how to manage their accounting purposes for business rides. 

Such conclusion and approach is also reflected in the guidance of [European Data Protection Board Guidelines|https://edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2021-07/eppb_guidelines_202007_controllerprocessor_final_en.pdf] (see p 82). 
# *How do we treat the fact of end user information upload to the Team Account?*
We treat such information sharing from Customer to Bolt being concluded between two separate controllers. When such information is uploaded to Bolt team account, then Bolt as a controller ensures compliance with the obligations stemming from data protection regulation. 
# *Can we accept being deemed as processor?* 
Yes, in practice we can accept a deviation from our standard approach of being a separate controller if the customer does not agree with our approach and it turns out to be a blocker for the deal. Then we specifically should limit the scope of data and purposes for which the customer would be deemed as controller. Also to limit the auditing rights etc in the agreement.

*Draft by Irena:*

*Step 1: Create a task within the project epic* {color:#36B37E}*[ DONE ]*{color} 

*Step 2: Schedule a 30 to 40-min session* {color:#36B37E}*[ DONE ]*{color} We did not have a call, but we thanked each other in DM messages and also had positive opinion about the whole project.

*Step 3: Analyse the project success* by reflecting on the following:

# *_What was the goal of the project?_*
Some units are outdated, missing relevant information, and lacks clarity.
With constant changes in the processes, procedures, and overall, the changes within the company - it becomes harder to keep up with small things, e.g. broken links and certain errors in the Onboarding course. Not monitoring it correctly can create issues in the future. The course has to be up-to-date with all the relevant details.
## *_What actually happened?_*
Overall, I think the project was a success, as it kept onboarding mostly up-to-date. Even with that, we received some other feedback that something was outdated, so imagine if we did not even do these regular grooming days.
Feedback from the agents and other users was very dependent on the month, so there was no consistency there. But, overall, we received more positive feedback than improvement action points. Also, some comments were very personal - some people would much rather want to have more videos, some quizzes and some said there were too many quizzes.
OSAT target of >90% was met in some months, but in the majority it did not and overall 2022 OSAT was 88%. I still think that is great, but in order to go over 90%, the onboarding should go over some structural changes, which is not what this project was about. This is simply to keeping it up-to-date, which served its purpose. So, although this criterion was not met, I think the bar was actually set too high. From the comments, you could see that there were a lot of comments on the onboarding structure, which is something that could be done in this project alone.
L&D task completion > 90% 
I calculated all of the tasks that should be done and were not rejected or postponed for certain reason. Tasks: 118, Done: 111. AVG: 94%
Target was met.
## _Were we accurate in predicting efforts?_
Yes, it was completed on time, we predicted the effort correctly. But, for Nov and Dec we had to prepare for New suppliers and also received a huge feedback from Transcom, thus it took more than expected.
## _What went well?_
I think the whole collaboration and managing the tasks went well and overall I think we accomplished what was planned.
## _What didn’t go well? How to avoid this the next time?_
When we updated certain information, we sometimes did not update it in all of the places it appears, thus causing confusion. This is because we were simply could not know where each information is, as onboarding was created/updated by several people and it is hard to keep track of who added what. I think this will be resolved by our team re-org, as we will have better overview of the whole onboarding. 
Updating bits here and there caused a bit of inconsistency, as some topics were reversed, which made no sense later. Also, everybody was updating it in their own way, which also cause different styles of PDFs and so on. A concrete action template should solve this - nothing too much, but just to keep the whole thing in thew same style and learning flow.
What I also realized is that we did not receive enough feedback or noticed all of the changes that happened, until some of OS trainers did not sent it to us. E.g. Courier profile in Admin changed a lot and nobody noticed until M+ trainers onboarding. We need to go through onboarding ourselves from time to time, or at least check some topics more. E.g. changes in Admin, which are not depicted in the KB.
## _What else can be improved?_
Well, for this project, nothing much. I think the way we did it worked very good. The general on boarding should be more organized and aligned with other LOBs, so we can use and link topics and simply be more aligned.

{noformat}    select
        rcvc.created,
        rcvc.created_hour,
        rcvc.session_id,
        rcvc.gps_lng,
        rcvc.gps_lat
    from (
        select
            created,
            created_hour,
            session_id,
            gps_lng,
            gps_lat,
            row_number() over (partition by session_id order by created asc) as rn
        from rental.rental_car_vehicles_by_categories
        where created_hour >= timestamp '{date_from}'
        and created_hour < timestamp '{date_to}'
        and city_id = 1
    ) rcvc
    where rn = 1{noformat}

Obviously this is a simplification as user could move. I’m also ignoring window coordinates ({{viewport_...}}). If a new session is triggered (bc timeout, user closes + reopens), I count this as distinct.

As a result, the following file was created, reviewing the current state of {{nodejs-common}} repo: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18oh5t65EVD3BfzUm7oqIcU9elHHH3PoyOg4y_9-kwqE/edit?usp=sharing|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18oh5t65EVD3BfzUm7oqIcU9elHHH3PoyOg4y_9-kwqE/edit?usp=sharing|smart-link] 

Key insights:

* Libraries highlighted in green were identified as core building blocks, meaning that most of other libraries build on top of them, and also developers can use them directly. This means that ideally those libraries wouldn’t depend on any other libraries than each other. As a result, we can create an action item that extracts each of those libraries under a separate {{tsconfig.json}}, which will greatly facilitate further splitting of {{nodejs-common}} repo under more individual folders with {{tsconfig.json}} in them. Ideally, we should arrive at a state where each of those libraries can be used on its own without requiring any extra {{nodejs-common}} dependencies, just like an arbitrary npm package.
* There’s a lot of ideas of splitting existing libraries into smaller chunks for better logical structure and dependency management.
* Libraries in yellow are all libraries which are currently initialized in {{NodeSetup}} during service startup, meaning that all of them have some global initialization code that needs to be run before using those libraries. Not sure how to use this information yet.
* It looks like some of the libraries could be unified under umbrella components, so that we wouldn’t end up with an overwhelming amount of components (if we were just to cover each subfolder with a separate component). For example, we could have a Caching component, which covers Cache, Redis, IMDS, and DataCache. Cache is related to Redis, since it uses it as its main strategy, and IMDS pairs well with DataCache, since they both handle {{DATA_NOT_MODIFIED}} in a similar fashion. It’s also important that the amount of knowledge and support covered by the component is manageable, so if all 4 libraries are a bit too much for a single component, we could also have “Redis Cache” and “In-memory cache”, which would cover Redis + Cache and IMDS + DataCache libraries respectively.
** In case there are libraries covering a similar area of responsibility, but not fitting under a single component, we can unite them by a common concept. For example, Kafka, MQTT and MQ (SNS/SQS/MqDbPublisher) are all about messaging, however each of the libraries has a formidable size to it, so it’s probably best to keep them as separate components. Yet, we can still assign a concept of “messaging” for each of those components, so that they would be more discoverable.
* Generator and component test framework both have a lot of functionality specific to other features. In case of component test framework, most of it already lives close to components, in {{ctest}} subfolders, but a small portion inside of {{src/componentTests/}} still could be split. As for the generator, almost each of its parsers and builders could be placed next to the component for which it is implemented. For now, we don’t need any plugin system, we just need to figure out the ownership, so we could start by assigning library-specific owners to individual builders and parsers, and eventually refactor the code by moving those builders and parsers under respective libraries.
* We can start by creating components for the libraries that have > 0 maintenance associated with it, as it will be most relevant in the nearest future, if say another request comes for such a library. There are some 0 maintenance components that look like they should belong to other teams, or it’s not clear if the current structure is the best one, but since they are basically maintenance-free, then there’s probably no point in touching them first, unless we need to touch them as a part of some other change.

Hey [~accountid:61c450c9f3037f006962ddd1] and [~accountid:61addb80b0b630006a695081], thanks for looping me in.

Good question. I analyzed it from the EU law perspective and it seems to be forbidden, although the intention is good. The EU Directive says in respect of self employed individuals the following: _The principle of equal treatment means that there shall be no discrimination whatsoever on grounds of sex in the public or private sectors, either directly or indirectly, for instance in relation to the establishment, equipment or extension of a business or the launching or extension of any other form of self-employed activity._ 

*Direct discrimination* means where one person is treated less favourably on grounds of sex than another is, has been or would be, treated in a comparable situation

*Indirect discrimination* means where an apparently neutral provision, criterion or practice would put persons of one sex at a particular disadvantage compared with persons of the other sex, unless that provision, criterion or practice is objectively justified by a legitimate aim, and the means of achieving that aim are appropriate and necessary

So, I don’t see any good defense strategy for us to move on with this one but [~accountid:61addb80b0b630006a695081] feel free to prove me wrong.

Hi there George!

To give a bit of context: The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are giving them a refund, therefore we are allowing them to financial gain and we are the ones who cause the fraud.

Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes. It is up to you how to action the eaters. 

Cheers,

Hi there Anna!

To give a bit of context: The fraud team deals with bigger cases of financial fraud or user patterns with a significant business case. The fraud team does not look at users on an individual level unless it is a clear false positive case. And even in those cases, it is rather for us to finetune our rules and restrictions for a more positive user experience for *good* users.

Further, what you have here is a *refund/promo fraud* (social engineering) case which, in general, is overall dependent on CS processes and procedures. Think of it this way - the user is just requesting a refund/promo and we are giving them a refund/promo, therefore we are allowing them to financially gain and we are the ones who cause the fraud.

Hence, I can suggest you follow your local processes in regard to users making bad reports/requesting refunds or compensations; and possibly raise this with your leads if you find issues with the processes. It is up to you how to action the user.

Cheers,

So definitely, there are just however two things to consider here, on how the item pricing works: 

We have Purchase Items and Inventory Items. Will describe the difference, as they are the same in theory, but in the system can act as two different things. So Purchase Items are like a catalog item from a supermarket, i.e. you see a crate of beer for €10, but those prices are constantly updated i.e. it might raise by €0.50 every few months and that means it would cost 10.50 a few months later.

Inventory Items are items that we hold in stock, with *average pricing* that are assigned at inventory site level*.* Which means that we can buy a front fork in January for 100 EUR, and then buy the same fork in June for 200 EUR. When we put-away these items into stock, the system will automatically calculate that the average price for this item is now 150 EUR. Slightly more complex logic around quantities, but that’s the simple version. 

So the question is the following: 

Do you have the requirement to see the Purchase Price for Items that we buy from suppliers (note that not all of them are filled out, as procurement has only gone live recently so the CN team is still updating a lot of the prices) or the Inventory Items that we have at Inventory Site level? Here are the answers to the Partner’s questions:

4.7. – Партнеру недостатньо відповіді в усному форматі, як ми будемо перевіряти процес надання послуг. Чи обгрунтовано це якось юридично? - _Bolt зацікавлений у належній якості харчових продуктів та послуг Партнера, які Партнер надає Клієнтам, тому у випадку скарг Клієнтів і т.д. Bolt залишає за собою право перевіряти процес надання послуг Партнером. Дане положення є стандартним положенням щодо аудиту, і спрямоване на належне надання послуг Клієнтом, в якому зацікавлені всі сторони._

5.9 - Коли і як ми повідомляємо партнерам про зміни описані в пункті? - _Зазвичай Bolt надсилає Партнеру електронний лист на електронну пошту Партнера, також документація між сторонами надсилається через сервіс “Вчасно“._ 

5.10 - Просять розʼяснення за яких умов можемо це робити. - _Bolt уповноважений надавати, а також скасовувати доступ Партнера до порталу партнерів Платформи Bolt Food у випадку порушення Партнером своїх зобовязань, технічної неможливості надати доступ до порталу і т.д. Партнер, який має доступ до порталу, уповноважений змінювати вміст розділу, присвяченого Партнеру._

6.2 - Що таке збір Маркетплейс? Як партнер його буде сплачувати? Який його можливий розмір? - _Збір Маркетплейс наперед не визначений і може застосовуватись з метою (і) покриття витрат на забезпечення доступності кур'єрських послуг на Маркетплейсі, або (іі) покладенні витрат на Партнера для забезпечення доступності кур'єрських послуг на Маркетплейсі. В разі застосування Збору Маркетплейс, Партнер все одно буде сплачувати лише Узгоджений відсоток Агентської винагороди (тобто комісію) як максимальну суму. Наприклад, Ціна замовлення становить 100 гривень, Агентська винагорода - 20% (тобто 20 гривень), а також стягується Збір Маркетплейс в розмірі 8 гривень. У такому випадку, ми зменшимо Агентську винагороду на 8 гривень, тому Партнер сплатить 8 гривень Збору Маркетплейс та 12 гривень Агентської винагороди. Разом 20 гривень, що дорівнює початково узгодженій Агентській винагороді._

7.6 - Просять розʼяснення щодо депозиту. - _Дане положення спрямоване на забезпечення повноти розрахунків у випадку здійснення готівкових платежів, проте на практиці наразі ми депозит не вимагаємо._

12.4, 12.5 - Просять розʼяснення, про які випадки йдеться. - _Дані положення спрямовані на забезпечення відшкодування Партнером на користь Bolt витрат, збитків і т.д., понесених Bolt у випадку порушення Партнером своїх зобов'язань._

12.8 - Про яке страхування йдеться? Де це зазначено в спеціальних умовах? - _Дане страхування наразі не передбачено Спеціальними умовами._

13.6 - коментар від їхного юриста щодо цього “Вони [ми - Bolt] не можуть самостійно визначати суд де буде розглядатись спір. Вніс зміни в спеціальні умови, які врегульовують це питання. - _Приймаємо зміни._

[~accountid:61151976ec92ab007046ccb7] thank you for the additional information this is really useful. The Danish Act on Restrictive Covenants states the following in the relevant section: 

_10. (1) An employer may terminate an agreement as referred to in Part 3 at one month’s notice for expiry at the end of a month._  
_(2) Upon termination according to subsection (1), the employee will be entitled to the lump sum referred to in section 8(3) and in section 9(2) upon resignation on the condition that the resignation takes place later than three months after the employee has commenced the employment and within six months after the employer terminated the agreement and the termination is due to circumstances that would have made the employer entitled to enforce the agreement._  

This means that he will still have the right to a lump sum compensation if the following three (3) conditions have been fulfilled: 

# the resignation takes place later than three months after the employee has commenced the employment, *AND*
# the resignation takes place within six months after the employer terminated the agreement (meaning after the non-compete has been terminated); *AND*
# The termination of the non-compete clause is due to circumstances that would have made the employer entitled to enforce the agreement (meaning that if we terminate the non-compete clause because the employee wants to take employment with a competitor then this would would have been a circumstance in which case Bolt could have enforced the non-compete clause. 

If all of these requirements are fulfilled he has a right to the two month lump sum as described in the employment contract and if not he has no right to such compensation. However, the current wording in the waiver only states that additional compensation will not be provided as far as permitted under Danish law. If you assess that such payment shall be made based on the above please clarify such wording. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Just to record that myself and [~accountid:613a01a1e2a0d60069d29ca1] went through and discussed the lease terms on Friday ahead of him meeting OLX next week in Berlin. Some remaining questions I have, in addition to the commentary in the G doc, for Merve to address when she is back from her leave: 

# How does the process of Head Landlord’s consent work in DE? I understand we have something informal - but is the formal consent obtained only once the agreement between us and the Landlord is signed? Is there any risk there that they could refuse their consent?
# What happens under German law when a Head lease is terminated - does the sublease also come to an end automatically? I see you have removed Clause 23 re Cessation - but what is the alternative if this is taken out - is this governed by the Civil Law and allows for the sublease to continue, with the Head Landlord becoming our Landlord? Or would a separate agreement need to be entered into?
# Linked to the above, there should be a provision in the lease which requires our Lessor to pay the rents and comply with the tenant obligations contained in the Head Lease - as it is in our interest to ensure that the Head Lease is not terminated (especially if our lease would also terminate automatically)? Or is this not usually included in DE?
# Clause 4.3 obliges us to obtain “all official permits and licenses” - what are these and what is involved in relation to being able to use the premises as an office? I ask because Clause 4.4 states that if any of these are refused - we will not be able to get out of the lease and nor will be able to use the lease? I propose to remove Clause 4.4 for that reason unless we are sure that there is nothing onerous in obtaining such permits before entry into the lease? Also will the office team in DE take charge in obtaining this? 
# I have not seen any reference to the Lessor or Head Lessor’s obligations to insure the Building? Is this covered by the Civil Law so does not require to be mentioned? I would expect that this would be covered by the Head Lessor in a multi let building, with us paying a pro-rata proportion through a service charge or equivalent. However I do see in Clause 12 reference to a rent suspension and a termination right if the property is damaged and will not be restored. Also [~accountid:613a01a1e2a0d60069d29ca1] please to reach out to our insurance team: Daniel Severin re the tenant’s insurance that we have to obtain pursuant to the lease terms - Clause 14. 
# I am a bit concerned by the VAT indemnity required from us in Clause 8.7 in respect of both the Lessor and the Head Lessor - would be good to understand if this is a market standard requirement in DE? Perhaps also the tax team can take a look at this? If we do decide to keep this - I have tried to soften the language a bit. Or alternatively could we agree some kind of a cap, as I have no idea what sums of money we are talking about here? But I imagine they could be substantial. 
# I am little bit confused about access rights and how this is typically dealt with in German leases - there is no express list of rights to use e.g. staircases, lifts etc and there is no definition of “Common Parts” which does not help matters. So unless this is somehow implied under Civil Law - best to set out expressly? I have put in clause 2.4 and 2.5 but please amend as is typical in DE. 
# Risto suggested a handover date of 15th of Feb - i.e. 2 weeks before the lease commencement. Perhaps first to agree this in principle with OLX and then adjust Clause 6 accordingly? This should be rent free early access so we can commence our fit out - we can pay utilities, that would be fair. 
# Re Clause 10 security deposit - understood that Risto is already in discussion with Mahmoud about this. I have not taken out the reference to the bank guarantee as the drafting says this is at our discretion. Just note that 2 weeks before handover is not looking realistic for us to provide this by. Best to speak to Mahmoud in terms of what is realistic. 

Best, 

Liisa

[~accountid:626fb920f42962006fde4c04] - I believe in Malta we have MTPL or Motor Third Party Liability with Gasan Mamo (GM). This is different to most of the countries we have cover in as MTPL is what is referred to as strict liability and hard to defend from a third party claim. It essentially the same as Motor Insurance on your car and therefore is always active - Unlike Rider General Liability (RGL) which is only active when associated to an active ride/trip.

Therefore, we could try and attempt to defend this incident and speak to the Legal about obtaining one of their letters they use for an RGL country. However, if might be best just to follow the CS procedure and pass this over to GM.

I believe Scooter incidents should be sent to: [carclaims@gasanmamo.com|mailto:carclaims@gasanmamo.com]

Hi there!

It seems we have two bigger cases piled here. While both are based on social engineering we should also look at them separately. 

The drivers are most likely phishing for OTP codes in order to use the riders' account and/or the payment method with the end goal of misusing the original owner's funds or bypassing some of our detection rules (that mostly target new accounts/accounts without good history). And the riders are most likely requesting driver information (especially email, phone number etc) to get access to driver earnings and/or account. 

The bad part is that this fraud excels due to the users giving a third party their personal information willingly, and we can’t physically stop someone from handing out such info. For example, it even says not to share the OTP code with anyone in the SMS the user receives.

Sadly, there is no concrete action we can take with social engineering other than suspending users who are directly related to the scheme. Another option would be to educate the drivers and riders about these schemes, however, this is difficult as well. We would look bad/as an unattractive service if we were to send out communication regarding bad drivers/riders on our platform. So it is a bit of a delicate subject in general. h3. How could we improve the model?

* Implement hyperparameter tuning, possibly optimising a different metric than AUC (eg average precision, F-metric)
* To extend it to other countries than South Africa (ZA), try global model (one for all countries) vs local models (one per country).
* In case of local models, I wonder if it could be worth to train each model considering only the top N types of safety tickets that account for e.g. 70-80% of the tickets in that country. The underlying principle would be to reduce the amount of different phenomena that the model tries to lear, in order to improve the performance on the most recurrent ones. Food for thought..
* Implement automatic retraining, possibly when observing model drift. We could start by comparing the performance of a run with the average performance of the previous N runs, and retrain if the performance is lower than a threshold. 
* Remove highly correlated features (e.g. avg_rating_last_month, avg_rating_last_3month) to possibly improve performance
* Feature pruning to improve maintainability of the model. This can be done by analysing how the performance of the model decreases when removing the least important features.

I am adding you to this ticket as I believe you may provide some clarity.

As Martim indicates in the ticket description, a BB client refuses to pay Bolt arguing that they receive the invoice from Bluwalk and also claim that this position is supported by Art. 63 of Lei Geral Tributária (*“LGT”*)

However, art. 63 LGT is about Tax Inspection and for me doesn’t support the client’s position, but as I am not a PT speaker, please correct me if I am wrong.

In contrast, I have found out that *Ofício Circulado N.º: 30213, de 2019-10-01  (*[*https://www.ivojoma.pt/docs/oc_30213_2019.pdf*|https://www.ivojoma.pt/docs/oc_30213_2019.pdf]*)* expressly regulates *self-billing and third-party invoicing* and says: 

*Self-billing and third-party invoicing*

_11. Invoices and other tax relevant documents may be drawn up by the acquirers of the goods or services ("self-billing") or_ +_by a third party in the name and on behalf of the taxpayer._+ _In either case, the taxpayer is responsible for issuing them and for the veracity of their content._ 

*Processing requirements*

_12. Article 7 of the Decree Law sets out some requirements to be observed in the processing of invoices and other tax relevant documents._

_12.1 Irrespective of the means of processing, invoices and other tax relevant documents shall be identified by their respective designations, being issued in one or series, conveniently referenced, dated and numbered in a progressive and continuous numbering within each series. Article 7(4) establishes a minimum period of one tax year for the duration of the series issued._

_These documents must include, as from 1 January 2020 20, a bar code (QR code) and a unique document code, under terms to be regulated by administrative rule._

_12.2 Invoices and other tax relevant documents processed through computer programs or computer programmes or other electronic means._

* _On invoices, all mandatory information must be inserted by the respective programme or equipment._

_In the documents that allow the conference of goods or services, the following elements must be inserted by the respective program or equipment:_

_"a) Sequential number of the document;_

_b) Date and hour of issuance;_

_c) Company name and tax identification number of the supplier of goods or service provider_

_d) Usual denomination and quantities of the transmitted goods or rendered services_

_e) The price net of tax and the amount of tax due, or the price including the tax_

_(e) the price net of tax and the amount of tax due, or the price inclusive of tax_

_f) Express indication that they do not constitute an invoice._

Hi Claire/Eanna, 

I hope you and the MHC/DLA team are doing well. 

This is a Request for Quote (RfQ) for your firm’s assistance to update Bolts Ireland Driver and Passenger Terms and Conditions.

*PASSENGER SERVICE FEE*

*Bolt Passenger Service Fee*

* We need our Passenger Terms and Conditions updated to enable a Passenger Service Fee to be charged to Bolt’s Passengers via our Bolt rider App. 
* In other jurisdictions this has been referred to as a Booking Fee or a Passenger Service Fee, please see our UK Passenger Terms and Conditions here for reference, however, we have elected to call this a ‘Passenger Service Fee’ for Ireland given it already has a legally required ‘Booking Fee’ allocated and we want to distance ourselves from competitors calling it a ‘Technology Fee’, see Ireland FreeNow’s Terms and Conditions here. 
* A red flag check has already been completed, see attached Dual Invoicing document for context. 
* Please simply copy and paste the PDF terms available from online and linked in this email to mark-up recommended edits. 

*Dual Invoicing* 

* In order to charge a Passenger Service Fee in Ireland, we want to implement Dual Invoicing for rides, both our Passenger and Driver Terms will need to be checked lightly to ensure they accommodate this model for 2023. 
* A ‘Dual Invoicing Model’ refers to an operating model for rides where:
** Passengers are charged by drivers for transport service (the “Transport Services”); and also
** Passengers are charged by Bolt for other services (the “Bolt Services” - inclusive of our Passenger Service Fee).
* Attached you will find our red flag check for Dual Invoicing in Ireland as well as an explanatory document from HQ which can provide further context (also attached).

*Fee charges and financial regulations in the EU*

* We are aware that legal complications can arise under EU financial regulations if we do not charge the Passenger Service Fee to cash payments but do charge this on electronic payments. 
* An issue we presently have is that our Bolt App does not yet accommodate the feature to charge a Passenger Service Fee on available cash payments in Ireland, to remedy this our product and engineering teams are working to fix this in coming weeks. 
* Whilst this App development is in progress, we will trial launching the Passenger Service Fee over a 4 week period where cash payments will be turned off entirely to reduce the risk of being penalised by financial regulators as Passenger Service Fees are charged per trip. 
* With the above developments in mind, please edit our Passenger TnCs to accommodate the following features: 
** Bolt is able to charge a Service Fee to Passengers for the company to use at its sole discretion (meaning it doesn’t have to go to the Driver, or any specific aspect of ‘Technology’ which FreeNow insinuates). We intend to use it mainly to boost driver bonuses for supply issues in Ireland - but we need fluidity on its use in case this strategy changes. 
** Bolt has complete discretion whether to enable payments made on the App via electronic means only or to provide electronic and cash payment options as we see fit (at any time). This is to safeguard our 4 week trial period when we turn off cash payments - but enables us to turn cash payments back on if we have the new App features available to charge a Passenger Service Fee electronically via the App alongside any Cash Payment. 
** Enable Dual Invoicing (as mentioned above)
** Ensure both the Passenger and Driver Terms and Conditions are flexible in language, in the event Bolt decides to withdraw/reverse the Passenger Service Fee all together and return to our former model of operation enabling electronic and cash payments. 

*Driver Terms and Conditions* 

* Please only complete a light check on our Driver Terms and Conditions to ascertain if amendments are in fact required to accommodate the Passenger Service Fee charged to Passengers. We need to ensure all terms mutually work for our above purposes, however, the UK terms did not require amendment here.
* In particular, we need to ensure these Driver terms also accommodate the Dual Invoicing system we would like to implement above, so they may need light amendments with this, please provide your recommendations (if any) in track changes - 4.18 for example will need to be checked. 
* Driver Terms and Conditions are here, simply copy and paste the text into a word doc for edits. 



*NEW CATEGORY - EXECUTIVE*

*Launching a new Limousine Category known as ‘Executive’ in Ireland*

Whenever the rider is charged for a ride (including cancellation fees), these sums will be added to driver’s gross earnings and the commission will be deducted at 15% (trips and cancellation fees). * Driver balance before the refund:

GROSS EARNINGS: 10€

NET EARNINGS: 8.5€

SPENDING: 1.5€ (Bolt commission)





* Driver balance after the refund:

GROSS EARNINGS: 10€

NET EARNINGS: -1.5€

SPENDING: 11.50€ (Bolt commission ; Refund to client)
